editorial:
Imagine what would happen if the most futuristic family in history bumped into the most prehistoric one. That is exactly what you get here. Elroy Jetson is a little genius who builds a time machine, but instead of a quick trip, he ends up landing right in the middle of Bedrock. It is a total clash of worlds where flying cars and robots meet dinosaurs and stone tools. The whole vibe is lighthearted and silly, making it the perfect kind of movie to put on when you just want to relax and laugh at some classic cartoon chaos.

What really works is seeing how the two families react to each other. The pacing is quick, and the jokes land well for both kids and adults. While the animation is a bit old school, it still has a lot of charm. If you are looking for a nostalgia trip, you should definitely check this out. You can easily find it for rent on Apple TV or stream it on Prime Video. If you really love these characters, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep this piece of animation history forever.
endingExplained: After all the crazy adventures and mishaps, Elroy finally figures out how to fix his time machine. The Jetsons say a heartfelt goodbye to Fred and Wilma Flintstone, promising to remember their stone-age friends. Elroy blasts off and flies back to the future, returning home safely to his parents. Everything goes back to normal in the future, but the families are left with a funny memory of their impossible meeting.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Hanna-Barbera cartoons and family comedies.
